5/5 Stars – Highly Recommend Luigi!

We had a fantastic experience working with Luigi as our general contractor for a renovation on our 1923 home in Rye. He came in right within our budget and stuck to the estimated timeline, which is impressive for any renovation, especially with an older property. Despite interviewing five other contractors, we’re so glad we chose Luigi and his team. His communication was excellent—he was always pleasant, responsive, and easy to reach by phone or in person.

Older houses always come with a few surprises, and sure enough, some small unforeseen issues came up during the project. Luigi handled every one quickly, professionally, and with zero drama—keeping everything on track without any stress.

We now trust him completely and can’t recommend him enough. If you’re looking for a reliable, skilled, and genuinely nice contractor who stays true to his word on budget and schedule, Luigi is the one to call!

Thank you, Luigi—we’re thrilled with the results!

ABOUT US

Luigi Building & Remodeling LLC is a licensed and insured general contracting company based in Mamaroneck, New York. Our mission is to deliver high quality construction services while maintaining transparency, reliability, and superior workmanship.

We collaborate with architects, engineers, and designers to execute projects
ranging from structural renovations to complete residential transformations.
Our experience managing multi-phase construction projects allows us to maintain
strict timelines, budgets, and quality standards.

Our reputation is built on professionalism, attention to detail, and the
ability to successfully deliver projects that increase both property value and
functionality.

How Our Remodeling Process Works
We've built a straightforward process that keeps you informed and in control at every stage, from the first conversation to the final walkthrough.

WHY HOMEOWNERS CHOOSE US
What Makes RNR Construction Different
Licensed and Insured
Wesley Reneer, Ben Ruiz, and Riley Reneer are all licensed general contractors in the state of Utah. Every project is fully covered from day one.
Dedicated Project Team
You get the same crew from start to finish, not a rotating cast of subcontractors. Consistent people means consistent quality and better communication.
Real-Time Project Tracking
We give every client access to project management software so you can see exactly what's happening on your project at any time. No more chasing your contractor for updates.
Locally Owned
RNR Construction is based in Provo. We live and work in the same communities as our clients. Our reputation here matters to us.
Transparent Pricing
We don't win jobs with low bids and make it up later. Your estimate is detailed, written, and accurate. If scope changes, we discuss it with you before the cost changes.
Financing Available
We offer construction financing through GreenSky so you can move forward now and pay over time. Ask us about financing options during your free estimate.

Our Story
Built by People Who've Worked in Construction Long Enough to Know What Goes Wrong
RNR Construction was founded in 2022 by Wesley Reneer and Ben Ruiz, childhood best friends who spent years working in construction before deciding to build something of their own. Installation Questions

Common Questions About the Installation Process.

Everything people typically ask before scheduling an installation.

Can you install a walk-in tub in a manufactured home?

In most cases, yes. Boca has installed in manufactured homes, condos, and a wide variety of home configurations. The key factors are existing plumbing access and bathroom dimensions. Your consultant will ask the right questions during your design session to confirm before you order.

Do you need to move walls or do any major remodeling?

In most standard installations, no. Boca Walk-In Tubs are designed to fit into the existing tub space without structural changes. In some situations — unusual plumbing configurations, very small bathrooms — minor modifications may be needed. We assess this and tell you upfront.

Do I need to do anything to prepare my bathroom before installation day?

Very little. Clear out personal items from around the tub area and make sure there's a clear path from your front door to the bathroom. Your installer handles everything else — including removing the old tub.

Does my water heater need to be upgraded?

For the Petite, Petite Short, and Standard models — no. A standard 40-gallon water heater is sufficient. For larger models, a tankless or 80-gallon water heater is recommended. Your consultant will flag this during your design session if it applies.

What if something isn't right after installation?

Call us — 800.903.8095. Boca's lifetime warranty covers the tub and the installation. Because we both built and installed your tub, there's no back-and-forth between companies. We come back, we make it right.

Can you install upstairs or in a second-floor bathroom?

Yes. Second-floor and upstairs installations are handled regularly. The logistics require some additional coordination, which your installer will walk you through. It does not affect the timeline in most cases.

About Bennett Contracting

Bennett Contracting is a full-service remodeling contractor dedicated to providing the highest level of service and craftsmanship to help improve existing homes and businesses in the Capital Region. With over 80 employees including carpenters, plumbers, electricians, designers, and office staff, we are prepared to help plan and design any remodeling project.

Founded in 1915 by Dan Bennett in Delmar, New York, the company evolved over 100 years from a small plumbing company to a full-service remodeling contractor. Dan’s sons-in-law grew the plumbing business into DA Bennett Heating & AC following WWII. One of Dan’s grandson’s, Greg Jackson, and childhood friend, Paul Gutman, established the DA Bennett Insulation division in the late 1970s. This division eventually broke off into its own company called Bennett Contracting, Inc. in 1984, and was led by Greg and Paul for over 40 years.

In 2019, Andrew Gutman and Kevin Gutman took over as the owners of Bennett Contracting. This transition plan was developed to ensure that the company is safely on its way to a second one hundred years in business. Firsthand involvement by the owners ensures that Bennett’s high standards are passed on to every customer on every project.

From kitchens and bathrooms to additions, windows, doors, siding, and outdoor living spaces, we help improve the comfort, function, and longevity of existing homes. Our approach is practical, collaborative, and grounded in how people actually live in their spaces.

Our Capital Region home remodeling services include:

The replacement of Windows, Doors and Siding
The design and renovation of Kitchens, Bathrooms and Basements
The design and building of Home Additions
The design and installation or renovation of Decks, Porches or Seasonal Rooms

We believe great remodeling is built on trust—and that trust is earned by doing what we say we’ll do, showing up when we say we will, and standing behind our work.

Our Purpose

At Bennett Contracting, our purpose is to serve our customers and employees with integrity and care, and to improve homes and uphold a century-long commitment to our community through exceptional craftsmanship.

Our Vision

To be the Capital Region’s most trusted name in home remodeling: where craftsmanship meets care, and every project begins a lasting relationship.

Our Mission

We transform houses into homes through expert design, quality construction, and personal service. With a hands-on approach and a collaborative mindset, we provide solutions and guide our clients through every step of the remodeling journey, delivering spaces they’re proud to live in and eager to share. We support our employees with a culture of teamwork, growth, and pride in our shared legacy.

Our Values

Since 1915, Bennett Contracting has been guided by values that shape how we work today.

Trust
We’ve earned our reputation over generations by doing what we say we’ll do, when we say we’ll do it.

Reliability
We offer dependability, stability and consistency to our customers and coworkers.

We hold ourselves to the highest standards of quality, from the jobsite to the office.

Service

Teamwork

Embrace Progress

100 Year History
Reliability. Trust. Quality. Value.

These are the ideas on which Bennett Contracting was first founded in 1915. As a third generation family run house contractor business based in Albany, NY, we are proud to stand behind the belief that every project, no matter how big or small, deserves our utmost attention and care. What began as a small plumbing business has currently expanded to a substantial company with a fleet of over 35 cars, trucks and trailers and 70 full-time professional employees.

Company Timeline

1915:  Dan (D.A.) Bennett opens a plumbing shop in a rented garage in Delmar, NY.

“Dan learned his trade as a steam fitter on the railroad.  In 1915 indoor plumbing and central heat were a “new thing” and he was able to take his skills and move into this new industry.  Things were simpler then, workers paid in cash at the end of the day and contracts written on the back of old envelopes.” 

-Greg Jackson, Co-Founder Bennett Contracting.

 

1945:  Dan’s sons-in-law Gill and Bud return form WWII and join the company, which becomes DA Bennett Plumbing & Heating.  The company enjoys strong post war growth along with the Bethlehem community.

 

1976:  Gil’s son Tom joins the company and at the suggestion of long time friend Paul Gutman starts an insulation business.  Greg Jackson, another grandson, joins to run the new insulation company, DA Bennett Insulation Company.

 

1978:  Paul Gutman join Greg Jackson as co-owners of the DA Bennett Insulation Company.

“At the time we started the insulation business we did less work in a year than we do now in a week.  Our office was a warehouse our office walls were bags on insulation.  We shared a double desk and single rotary phone, if you needed a photo copy you took a dime and went to the library.”  

-Greg Jackson, Co-Founder Bennett Contracting.

 

1984:  Paul and Greg become the sole owners of the newly named Bennett Contracting, Inc.  They move the business to their current location at 693 S Pearl St in Albany, NY.

“During these years the company came of age and grew from 10 employees to over 70 today.  It expanded beyond insulation into a full-service remodeling firm, with the development of our insurance, commercial, and home remodeling services.  Our kitchen and bath business increased 1000%.  We have since added adjacent land and built offices, showroom and warehousing.” 

-Paul Gutman, Co-Founder Bennett Contracting.

 

1990’s & 2000’s: The business grows and expands into new products and services. Beyond just windows and insulation, the company enters into residential general contracting and commercial renovations. The office and field staff increase to around 50 employees by 2010.

 

2010: Ground is broken on Bennett Contracting’s first major office expansion. A 3-story addition is added, providing space for a new showroom, more offices and meeting space in the basement.

 

2016: Bennett’s evolution leads to bringing design in house. Our first designer, Justina Auer, joins the team and Bennett becomes a dealer of cabinets and countertops in order to support to support their robust remodeling projects. This allows for Project Manager to take full control of the projects from start to finish, without the need for relying on third parties.

 

2019: Andrew and Kevin Gutman purchase the business from Paul Gutman and Greg Jackson, entering its fourth generation of ownership for the Bennett brand. The company stands at about 75 employees and has garnered an exceptional reputation in the region for home renovations.

“We are committed to continue our 100 plus year tradition of quality and integrity in the remodeling and renovation business.  Dedicating ourselves to the success of our employees and the service of our customers, neighbors, and friends.”

-Andrew Gutman, President Bennett Contracting.

OUR PROCESS

First Steps

It all begins with an idea! If you want your dream home to come to life, complete our form to schedule a phone consultation. If we’re a good fit, we will set up an in-person (or Zoom) consultation within 1-5 days.

During the call, you will have the opportunity to speak your mind on design ideas and layouts. After completing the consultation, we will provide a detailed estimate* and a 2D drawing of your project within 4 days (larger projects will require a few more days).

*There will be a fee for this estimate that will go toward your project if we are a good fit.

Design Agreement Phase

Once we've created an agreed upon estimate, that brings us to the design agreement. This is where the fun starts! In this phase, you will be supplied with virtual 4k rendered walk throughs of your project, as well as partner with our in-house design team to bring their vision to reality. This means we walk side by side with you through our best vendors and help design your project from floor to ceiling. 

Our goal is to create a space that reflects your style and that you are proud to call home, thus our vision statement - "New Home, Same Address". In this stage, we focus on helping you finalize a  design that you fall in love with.

Construction Begins

Once all design selections are finalized and material is delivered, construction begins! Through our online project portal, Co-construct, our project manager will send you a schedule with a tentative start date. 

Co-construct is a great resource we use to keep in communication about your project. This includes messages, updates, photos, inspiration, and more.

Project Completion

When the project is complete, we'll do a final walk through and take photographs!  We trust that our project manager and closely-knit tradesmen will work hard to make your dream home a reality. We’d love to get to know you and hope to make your dream home a reality. We are a company where high quality craftsmanship and custom design meet.

Kitchens and storage solutions,

Born in Copenhagen in 2014, we create kitchens and storage solutions that make everyday life beautifully better.

 

Together with some of the world’s leading designers and architects, including David Chipperfield, Norm Architects, Jean Nouvel, Muller Van Severen, Inga Sempé, and Cecilie Manz, we offer collections that blend Scandinavian simplicity with global ideas, bringing character and cohesion to your home. 

 

We guide you from the first sketch to the final installation, creating spaces that feel considered and made for the way you actually live. 

 

Our Scandinavian approach is about warmth without excess, natural materials chosen for how they look, feel, and age, and the conviction that beautiful design shouldn’t belong to the few. We create solutions that feel personal, not perfect. As a B Corp-certified company, every Reform kitchen and storage solution is made to order in Northern Europe. Read more about our production and sustainability.

Why Master Hand Construction Services

Your remodel shouldn’t become your second job.

A remodeling project can involve construction, plumbing, electrical work, layouts, fixtures, materials and dozens of decisions that affect one another. When those pieces are treated as separate jobs, the homeowner often becomes the person connecting them.

Master Hand Construction Services is built differently. Our construction, plumbing, electrical and design expertise stay part of the same conversation, so decisions are made around the project as a whole.

One connected team
Less passing the project from one unrelated trade to another. The people involved understand what the other parts of the job need.
Better-informed decisions
A layout doesn’t exist separately from plumbing. Lighting doesn’t exist separately from electrical. Materials don’t exist separately from budget. We look at those decisions together.
Communication that keeps you involved
You should be able to ask questions, understand why a decision matters and know what happens next.
A personal connection, start to finish
Our team stays involved from planning through completion, with a trusted team member coordinating the work and keeping you informed.

Our story

A family-owned contractor with decades of hands‑on experience.

Craftsmanship shaped in Central New York. A family business built in Tennessee.

Dan LeClair
Co-founder · General Construction and Plumbing
Crystal LeClair
Co-founder · Interior Design and Management

Master Hand Construction Services is a family-owned company. It is run by Dan and Crystal LeClair, and it is built around a straightforward idea: do good work, communicate clearly, and build relationships that last beyond one project.

Everything started when Dan learned the trades in Central New York alongside his grandfather, a home builder and cabinet maker. He started his first construction business at 18 and built his career around craftsmanship, problem-solving, and helping clients understand what was happening in their homes.

Crystal has been seeing spaces differently since she was a child, making mood boards and reimagining rooms long before she could build any of it. Her interest in design grew alongside an interest in what sits behind the walls, and years in real estate taught her how people actually use a home and what a renovation does to its value. In the company routine, she works alongside him in the management of the company, project development, client experience, and design.

Together, they stay closely connected to the projects Master Hand Construction Services takes on, and the company is small and family-owned by choice. Clients are not passed from department to department. The people you meet are the people invested in the project, the workmanship, and the reputation attached to the name.

Welcome! I’m Keith.               

“Work hard in silence, and let success be your noise.”

Guilty as charged! I’m originally from the Midwest - Channahon, just south of Chicago. I’ve been fortunate to work in a variety of fields and live a few lives. (Ask me about culinary!)

But those close to me know my favorite job is being a dad and husband.

My wife and I moved to Colorado in 2018, and we raise our three kids in Brighton. When not on the jobsite, I'm likely serving at church, hanging at a park with the kids, or whipping up something fun for dinner. 

As the founder and owner of CCR, I hold our general contracting license and meet individually with each client. 

My biggest strength in advising homeowners comes from understanding spatial potential. I can walk into a room and see what it can become. I love sitting down with potential clients, hearing how they live in their home, and designing solutions that fit the way their family uses the space. 

Feel free to schedule a meeting, and I look forward to starting your project!

MEET WITH KEITH
Cook Construction & Renovation’s Story:

In the wake of the pandemic, our founder Keith took a leap of faith and started a construction company to support his wife and three small kids. What began as a bathroom remodel for his pastor has grown into a trusted Colorado construction firm with 80+ clients. 

Keith works directly with every homeowner -- and not just as a contractor, but also as a partner who listens, designs your vision, and keeps you in the loop at every step. If you have worked with us, you know: we over-communicate on purpose. Your home is your family's safe place, and we treat it that way. 

We complete whole-home remodels, residential additions, basement renovations, master suite transformations, and custom built-ins. We are especially loved by young families and longtime homeowners who value trust, transparency, and craftsmanship. We have an A+ rating with the Better Business Bureau, a 5-star rating on Google and Facebook, and a list of referrals from happy and loyal customers.

The Trueson Team Timeline
2010
The Start of TrueSon Exteriors & Interiors
Barry Roewe, owner of TrueSon Exteriors & Interiors was at a pivotal moment. Continue down the path of working for someone else, or take the biggest risk of his career. And while Barry is not the type to shy away from a challenge, starting a new business was not an easy choice. He saw the industry from the perspective of a successful salesperson, but he knew he could offer more. And while building those initial relationships with people might be one of the more difficult parts of starting a business, this was an area Barry was most comfortable. In 2010, Barry made the leap. This was the start of TrueSon Exteriors & Interiors, though the original name was TrueSon Exteriors.
2012
From "Solopreneurship" To Entrepreneurship
Barry spent 2010 – 2012 doing mostly everything on his own including hand writing proposals late into the evening with his newborn, Mason, laying beside him. Along with proposals, Barry was also scheduling each project and being very hands-on from start to finish with each customer and sub-contractor. It wasn’t until 2012 that Barry had finally built his small business up to a level where he felt comfortable bringing someone on full time. Enter, Brian Davis, TrueSon’s first official employee. Brian was the Installer piece of the puzzle that elevated TrueSon’s business model from all sub-contracted work to some in house production. Together, Barry and Brian would continue offering that exceptional level of customer service that customers were accustomed to, but they could also control the quality of the service provided through Brian’s exceptional craftsmanship.

2013
The TrueSon Family continues to expand
In 2013, Barry and Brian had built up enough of a customer base that it was time to hire someone to manage home-base. Kara Parish was hired to manage the accounting and clerical work and she did this from Barry’s personal home. She eventually upgraded her office to the shop outside of Barry’s home in the middle of rural Ashland, Missouri. 2014 saw the addition of Chris Sivert and Nevada Shelkey. Chris was hired to measure and order material, deliver materials to job sites and coordinate with sub-contractors. Nevada was TrueSon’s first sales team member. With Sivret and Shelkey, the company had grown to 11 employees including 7 crew members, 1 admin, 1 production team member, and 2 sales representatives, officially outgrowing Barry’s personal shop. The TrueSon family found a new home in a rented space on the South side of Columbia, Missouri.

2015
Growing Into Interior Remodeling And Additions
In 2015, the company took another big leap when Barry recognized the local market was in need of a quality Interior Remodeling and Additions company. With that in mind, he connected with long-time friend, Tyler Kallenbach. Tyler grew up renovating his childhood home with his father and had been successfully running his own remodeling company. Barry and Tyler had a mutual respect for each other’s work ethic and attention to detail. TrueSon Exteriors was growing into a full-service construction company.

2017
Bringing On The Best In The Construction Business
The TrueSon family would continue to expand over the next couple years. As the TrueSon brand and reputation grew, Barry recognized the need to continue bringing on the best in the business. The thought process of having in-house crews would allow Barry to control and elevate the quality-of-service TrueSon could provide. In 2017, TrueSon brought on Doug Strodtman. Doug headed up the first in-house Deck crew. In 2018 Barry hired his first in-house Siding crew headed by Johnny Bargas and Alex Tripaldi. Every TrueSon crew was hand-picked. Each crew was built of highly motivated individuals, with great character, and a passion for doing things the right way. One of Barry’s greatest successes has been his ability to hire the right people. With the increase in Production Teams and jobs covering the job board, Chad Adkins was brought on in 2020. Adkins’ ability to keep track of all the moving parts, scheduling jobs, and handling the crews immediately elevated productivity.

2021
Highlighting The TrueSon Production Teams
In 2021 TrueSon brought in Gary Tegerdine. Tegerdine made an instant impact from an accounting perspective, but he also brought a strong set of management skills into the fold. Tegerdine was quickly promoted to the General Manager role giving Barry someone on site to help manage the team and improve company-wide communications. 2021 also brought the addition of Jeff Blumer, an in-house Marketing & Design Specialist. Blumer has given the company and brand improved visibility, highlighting the talented TrueSon Production Teams with his photography and videography while also writing an entertaining blog and newsletter.

Trueson operates by a set of core values
Accountability
Accountability is rooted in the understanding that our actions impact those around us.
It’s a daily effort of owning the way we show up and the decisions we make.
Accountability is the bridge between commitment and results.
It’s embracing that you are both the issue & the fix of the matter. Pointing fingers is only a distraction from moving forward.
When we hold each other accountable, we remind each other, “You’re capable of a bigger game.”
To put it simply, we have two options: We either make ourselves accountable or we will be made accountable by our circumstances.
Excellence
Excellence is a mindset. It’s not about talent, skill, or competence.
It’s merely choosing to hold yourself to a higher standard.
Excellence is a process. There’s no arrival point.
When we’re always striving for better, we raise the bar for ourselves and those around us.
Through this consistent endeavor, together, we move beyond mediocrity into greatness.
Integrity
Integrity is the quality of being honest.
A home is intimate, and it’s our responsibility to be trustworthy.
Integrity is taking action based on values rather than personal interests.
It’s choosing to do the hard thing over what is fast or easy.
When we act this way, trust is the byproduct.
With integrity comes freedom. When you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear.

Lift your teammates.
Plan forward.

Excellence

Embrace the chaos.
Think grey.
Be passionate & have fun.

Integrity

A great design isn’t just about change—it’s about transformation. Our Before & After gallery showcases the dramatic impact of thoughtful planning, skilled craftsmanship, and high-quality materials.

Whether it’s a complete home remodel, a modernized commercial space, or a stunning exterior makeover, these projects prove what’s possible when vision meets expertise.

Explore the transformations and imagine what we can do for you!

Transformations That Inspire
Kitchen Remodel – Moose Lake, MN
Before
After

These Moose Lake, Minnesota homeowners wanted a modern, functional kitchen to replace their outdated and inefficient layout. The original island, with two small peninsulas, created a bottleneck, while the new design features a more open and accessible workspace. Relocating the refrigerator to the opposite wall also provided a larger prep area next to the stove, improving both flow and functionality.

Park Point Screen Porch Remodel – Duluth, MN

This Park Point screen porch was in dire need of an upgrade, with inadequate framing that didn’t meet modern codes and a worn-out appearance. J&RS completely rebuilt the structure, reinforcing the framing and updating the siding and windows, transforming it into a fresh, secure, and stylish space.

Before
After
Stairway Remodel – Duluth, MN
Before
After

While the existing staircase was already elegant, these homeowners wanted a more modern, industrial aesthetic. J&RS helped them achieve this bold transformation with white skirt and riser boards paired with black treads for striking contrast, while sleek steel cable railings completed the contemporary industrial look.

Deck Renovation – Carlton, MN

For this deck renovation in Carlton, MN, we upgraded the space with low-maintenance composite decking for lasting durability and easy upkeep. Sleek Westbury aluminum railings add a modern touch while ensuring safety, and new composite stairs provide a seamless connection from the driveway to the deck. To complete the transformation, vinyl lattice skirting was added around the perimeter for a polished and refined look.

Before
After
Lakeside Bathroom Remodel – Duluth, MN
Before
After

J&RS helped these homeowners update their Lakeside bathroom with a new tile floor, fresh paint, upgraded fixtures, and a custom tile walk-in shower replacing the old fiberglass unit. The result is a modern, refreshed space that blends style and functionality.

Lakeside Master Bathroom Shower Remodel – Duluth MN

These homeowners turned to J&RS to transform their outdated, cramped bathroom into a modern, open space. By removing interior walls, J&RS created room for a fully tiled walk-in shower. Sleek white 8″ hex tiles flow seamlessly from the walls into the shower, while glass shower walls add brightness and sophistication.

Stories of Craftsmanship & Innovation
Reliable Insurance Office
About Reliable Insurance Office

When Reliable Insurance outgrew their space, they needed a new office that combined function with a fresh, welcoming feel. We reimagined their new building into a workspace that encourages both focus and connection, adding private offices, sound-insulated meeting rooms, and comfortable shared areas. The result is a space that reflects their friendly, hometown spirit—while giving their team room to grow.

Our Solution

We gutted Reliable’s newly acquired building to start fresh, rebuilding with dedicated offices, sound-insulated meeting rooms, and inviting spaces that support their close-knit team culture. A modern mix of materials was used throughout, with special attention given to the front reception area for a bold first impression. The expanded breakroom now comfortably hosts the entire team for potlucks and hockey tournament watch parties—making Reliable not just the friendliest, but possibly the coolest insurance company in town.

London Road Rooftop
About London Road Rooftop

This 3,540-square-foot home on London Road in Duluth, MN, underwent targeted outdoor renovations to restore weather-worn areas and enhance both function and style. Work focused on revitalizing the balcony, garage roof, and decking to better integrate with the home’s structure and support the residents’ lifestyle.

Our Solution

J&RS approached the deck and roof repair with precision, beginning with full demolition and a temporary support wall. New joists, sheathing, and high-density insulation improved durability and energy efficiency, while a 60-mil EPDM rubber membrane provided superior waterproofing. Ipe wood tiles on a Bison pedestal system were installed for a low-maintenance, resilient deck, and the existing iron railing was reinstalled with new scuppers and steel flashing to improve drainage. The result is a safe, stylish, and long-lasting outdoor space.

East Hillside Remodel
About East Hillside Remodel

This Duluth home, affectionately called an “Urban Cabin,” was selected for its charm and the promise of capturing the warmth of early married life. To better accommodate gatherings, the layout was reimagined to create an open, welcoming space that balances functionality with a cozy, inviting feel.

Our Solution

To bring this vision to life, the layout was reimagined by relocating the kitchen to the heart of the home, creating a welcoming space for gathering and conversation. An underused back room became a bright sunroom—ideal for relaxing or working—turning the cabin into a warm, versatile hub for everyday living and entertaining.

WHAT TO EXPECT
About Our Process

We understand the importance of transparency and communication, which is why we'll keep you informed throughout the process. We’re here to guide you through every step — from initial design to final reveal.

STEP 1
Initial Consultation Call

This is where we listen to your vision, understand your requirements, and discuss the potential of your project. We believe every home tells a story, and we're here to help yours unfold.

STEP 2
In-Home Evaluation

Following our discussion, we'll schedule a visit to your home to assess the space, take necessary measurements, and provide you with a more accurate proposal.

STEP 3
Design & Build Services

We offer comprehensive design services to bring your ideas to life. From selecting the right materials to choosing the perfect layout, our team will strive to listen to and implement your vision.

STEP 4
Project Schedule

We'll provide you with a detailed timeline for your project through the Buildertrend app. We'll keep you informed throughout the entire process. Our goal is to ensure that your project is completed on time and within budget.

STEP 5
Quality Assurance

Quality is at the heart of everything we do. As your project progresses, we'll conduct regular check-ins to ensure that everything is proceeding according to plan and meeting our high standards and your satisfaction.

STEP 1.
Choose the Consultation That Fits Your Project

At TBrothers, we go beyond quick estimates and rushed walkthroughs.

A successful renovation begins long before construction starts. The foundation is clarity—clarity in layout, design direction, scope, structural needs, and realistic budgeting.

Some homeowners already know their layout and simply need accurate pricing. Some want full design support before committing. Others are still exploring ideas and need guidance.

Choosing the right consultation ensures you get real value—not a generic “ballpark” number that leads to surprises later.

Our consultations are different.

Our consultations are an investment in getting your project right from the start.

Most contractors spend 10–15 minutes in your home, take a quick look, and give you a number without:

Taking measurements
Evaluating mechanical systems
Reviewing layout feasibility
Discussing finish levels
Addressing structural considerations

Then once work starts, the change orders begin:

“That’s not included.”
“We didn’t price for that.”
“This will be extra.”

Suddenly the “cheap” quote becomes the most expensive mistake.

Our process ensures you get real value

You’re not getting a quick number. You’re getting accuracy, transparency, and peace of mind.

We take the time to understand your needs, walk the space thoroughly, ask the right questions, and build a detailed scope and preliminary budget based on what we can clearly see and reasonably anticipate.

While no contractor can see through walls or guarantee that hidden conditions won’t appear, our process minimizes surprises because we do the due diligence up front.

The only surprises that arise are true unknowns—conditions no contractor could identify until demolition begins.

A. IN-HOME CONSULTATION — $125
Most Popular — Best for homeowners who already have a layout, plans, or a strong direction.

Choose this option if you:

Already know your general layout
Are working with a designer or architect
Have plans, drawings, or inspiration ready
Know your preferred styles or materials
Want a realistic, detailed budget before committing

During this visit, we will:

Evaluate your space in person
Identify visible structural, plumbing, or electrical considerations
Discuss your goals, finishes, and investment range
Provide a realistic preliminary budget (not a ballpark guess)
Outline the next steps and what’s required for accurate planning

If you already have a designer or architect:

We work seamlessly alongside your existing design team. After the consultation, we provide a checklist of specifications needed, coordinate on layouts and materials, and clarify what TBrothers will handle during construction.

Turnaround: 7–14 days for your preliminary budget.

Book Your In-Home Consultation
B. IN-HOME DESIGN CONSULTATION — $450
Best for homeowners starting from scratch or wanting a fully visualized design before construction.

Choose this option if you:

Need professional design guidance on finishes and materials
Are reconfiguring your layout or exploring different design paths
Want both design and accurate construction pricing in one process
Prefer to see 3D renderings before committing to construction

You receive:

A full in-home walk-through with detailed measurements

Frequently Asked Questions About Basement Finishing in Utah

Key Takeaways

Basement finishing turns unfinished square footage into usable living space without changing your home’s footprint.
Utah homes are built with basements more often than homes in most states, and Utah households are the largest in the country.
Permits are required, and requirements vary by city across the Salt Lake Valley.
Timelines depend on scope, permitting, and material lead times rather than a fixed schedule.
A finished basement can serve as a family room, guest suite, home theater, office, or basement apartment.
Cost depends on square footage, whether you add a bathroom, and the finishes you choose.
The right basement contractor manages permitting, trades, and inspections, so you don’t have to coordinate them yourself.

You already own the square footage. It is sitting under your house holding boxes and a water heater, and finishing it is the most common remodel Utah homeowners take on.

Utah has a specific reason for that. Households in Utah have an average of 3.08 people, the highest of any state, so families run out of room faster than the house was designed for.

This covers what homeowners actually ask us about basement remodeling across Draper, Sandy, South Jordan, West Jordan, and the rest of the Salt Lake Valley. When you want numbers for your own project, the basement cost calculator is the place to start.

In this post, you’ll learn:

What basement finishing actually involves, phase by phase
Whether you need a permit, and why it varies by city
What Utah homeowners put in a finished basement
How to choose a contractor and what to look for
What Does Basement Finishing in Utah Involve?

Basement finishing in Utah usually starts with an unfinished basement that has concrete walls, exposed framing, and rough utilities.

The sequence rarely changes. Design comes first, then permitting, then the parts that get covered up, then everything you actually see.

Phase	What happens
Design and planning	Layout, material selections, and scope get defined before anything is ordered
Permitting	Plans go to your city for review and approval
Framing and rough-ins	Walls go up, then electrical work, plumbing, and HVAC
Inspections	The city signs off before anything gets covered
Insulation and drywall	Walls get closed, taped, and textured
Finishes	Flooring, trim, paint, fixtures, and cabinetry
Final walkthrough	Punch list and closeout

Utah basements add one consideration most states do not. Below-grade space swings between cold winters and dry summer heat, so insulation and sealing matter more than they would in a milder climate.

How Long Does a Basement Project Take?

There is no standard answer, and anyone who gives you one before seeing your basement is guessing. A basement project timeline depends on three things you control and one you do not.

What moves the schedule:

Scope. A single open family room finishes faster than a basement with a bathroom, a wet bar, and three bedrooms.
Permitting. Review times vary by city, and that queue is outside anyone’s control.
Material lead times. Flooring, cabinetry, and specialty fixtures all have their own schedules.
Change orders. Deciding to add a bathroom halfway through resets part of the sequence.

Project management is what keeps it moving. A dedicated project manager coordinates trades, schedules inspections, and manages sequencing so the drywall crew isn’t waiting on an electrician who was never scheduled.

Do You Need a Permit to Finish a Basement in Utah?

Yes. Finishing a basement adds living space, requires electrical and plumbing work, and creates rooms where people sleep, so every city in Utah requires permits and inspections.

Requirements differ by city. Draper, Sandy, South Jordan, West Jordan, and Salt Lake County each have their own submission process, review timelines, and inspection scheduling, so what applied to your neighbor’s project may not apply to yours.

Egress and What Inspectors Look For

Egress is the requirement people miss. Any basement bedroom needs a window or door large enough to escape through, and adding one usually means cutting concrete and building a window well.

A fully licensed and insured general contractor handles this for you. That means pulling the permits, scheduling inspections at the right stages, and making sure the work passes before it gets covered.

What Do Utah Homeowners Use a Finished Basement For?

Basement finishing in Utah gives you rooms that the rest of the house doesn’t have space for. What goes down there depends on who lives in the house and what they keep running out of room for.

The most common uses:

Family room. The big open space where kids and their friends end up, and the reason most Utah families finish a basement at all.
Guest bedroom or guest suite. A bedroom and bathroom that gives visitors somewhere to stay without displacing anyone.
Home theater. Below grade is naturally darker and quieter, which makes it the right place for it.
Home office or gym. Functional living spaces that need separation from the rest of the house.
Basement apartment. A separate entrance, kitchen, and bathroom, which comes with its own permitting requirements.

Most finished basements combine two or three of these. A family room with a bathroom and one guest bedroom covers what most households need, and it leaves room to change the layout later.

For more on what works, our post on finished basement ideas walks through real Utah layouts.

What Does Basement Remodeling Cost in Utah?

The cost of basement finishing in Utah depends on three things. Square footage, how many rooms you are adding, and what you choose for materials.

Bathrooms and kitchens drive the cost more than anything else. Adding plumbing where none exists means new supply lines, drains, and venting, and a basement apartment with a full kitchen is a different project than an open family room.

Get a Number Built Around Your Basement

Finishes carry the rest of the budget. Premium materials for flooring, cabinetry, and fixtures can double the cost per square foot compared to standard selections, and that choice is entirely yours.

Rather than quote a range that will not match your basement or your budget, run your own numbers. The basement cost calculator uses your square footage and the rooms you want to give you a starting point tailored to your project, not someone else’s.

How Do You Choose a Basement Contractor?

The basement contractor you hire determines how the whole project goes. Licensing and insurance are the floor, not the qualification.

What separates one from another:

Basement experience specifically. Below-grade work involves moisture, egress, and mechanical systems that a kitchen remodeler may not handle regularly.
A defined scope and budget upfront. You should know what is included and what is not before anyone starts.
A named project manager. Someone whose job is coordinating trades and inspections, not a phone number you hope answers.
Real references in your area. Contractors who work throughout the Salt Lake Valley can point you to nearby finished basements.

Ask how they handle problems. Every project hits something unexpected, and the difference in quality shows up in how a team communicates when that happens rather than when everything is going well. There is more to weigh when choosing a basement finishing contractor.

Is a Finished Basement a Good Investment?

A finished basement is a good investment for a specific reason. Basement finishing in Utah adds square footage to a house that already has the foundation and roof, so you are not expanding the structure, only completing what is already there.

Demand is part of it too. Utah grew 18.4% over the last decade, the fourth-fastest rate in the country, and more people means more pressure on the housing that already exists.

The practical value comes first. A basement apartment can generate rental income, a guest suite means family stops staying in hotels, and a family room downstairs keeps the main floor from being the only place anyone can be.

Why Permitted Work Matters at Resale

A finished basement completed with permits and inspections counts toward the square footage on record. One finished without them does not.

Talk to your neighbors before you commit. In most Salt Lake Valley neighborhoods, somebody nearby has already done this, and their experience with a specific contractor is worth more than any review.

How Basement Finishing Fits With Other Home Remodels

Basements often get finished alongside other work. If you are already remodeling your home room by room, combining projects can save you a second round of permitting, scheduling, and having crews in the house.

The overlap is real. A basement bathroom and an upstairs bathroom share plumbing decisions, and flooring ordered for both at once means one delivery and one installation window.

Planning the Sequence

Thoughtful design up front prevents rework. Deciding layout options for the whole house before anyone starts framing means the basement is planned around how you will actually use the rest of the home.

One process, one schedule, one point of contact. Remodeling basements as part of a larger project works when a single team manages the whole thing, and it goes badly when three contractors each manage their own piece.

More Questions Utah Homeowners May Ask
Can you finish a basement that is only partially framed?

Yes, and it often saves time. If a previous owner framed walls or ran rough plumbing, an inspection confirms what is usable and what must be removed before the rest of the work is scoped.

Do you need to move out during the project?

Almost never. Basement work stays below grade, and a contractor who manages dust control and access can keep the rest of the house livable throughout the process.

What about moisture and radon?

Both get addressed before finishing. Utah basements are drier than in many states, though sealing, drainage, and radon testing should be part of the plan rather than done after the drywall goes up.

Can you add a bathroom where there is no plumbing?

Usually yes. It requires cutting the concrete slab to run drains, which is more involved than adding an upstairs bathroom, and it is routine work for a team that regularly does basements.

How do you handle ceiling height?

Existing height is what you have. A good layout works around ductwork and beams by placing them over hallways and closets rather than in the middle of a family room.

What if your budget does not cover the whole basement?

Finish it in phases. Framing and rough-ins for the full space now, then finishing rooms as the budget allows, keeps the process simple and avoids paying twice for the same work.

What a Basement Contractor Handles That You Would Not

A basement project has more moving parts than it looks like from the top of the stairs. Most of the work is coordination, and that is what a general contractor is actually for.

Where the work happens:

Permitting and inspections. Submitting plans to your city, scheduling inspections at the right stages, and making sure work passes before it gets covered.
Sequencing the trades. Framers, electricians, plumbers, HVAC, drywall, and finish carpenters each have to arrive in order and not wait on each other.
Catching what is behind the walls. Existing plumbing, ductwork, and structural posts all shape the layout, and finding them after framing is expensive.
Managing the budget through changes. Every project hits a decision that was not in the original scope, and how it’s priced and approved matters.

A team that does basements regularly has hit all of this before. The process is the same every time, which is why it remains predictable rather than becoming a series of surprises.

Get Answers About Finishing Your Basement

Basement finishing in Utah starts with knowing what your project involves. Square footage, the rooms you want, and the finishes you choose all affect the number, and none of that is guesswork once you put real inputs into it.

Use the basement cost calculator to get a starting point built around your basement rather than a state average. It takes a few minutes and gives you something concrete to bring to a conversation.

The Owner’s Suite: Before

The existing bathroom was past its prime: the large soaking tub consumed most of the bathroom space, making it feel cramped. The homeowners wanted a more simplified and sophisticated bathroom and owner’s suite with an oversized shower, a refreshed vanity with new fixtures and more storage.

The Owner’s Suite: After

Removing the soaking tub, stall shower and wall makes room for the oversized shower. The window above the old soaking tub is replaced with a transom window above the new shower for natural light and privacy.

Custom and stock cabinetry upgrade the vanities, keeping the same orientation. Smaller-trimmed mirrors look more polished and allow room for artwork. Under the vanities, drawers and rollouts provide easy-access storage, with neutral colors and fixtures throughout to create a calm, serene aesthetic.

Removing the wall between the original tub and shower allows us to expand the closet space. Custom cabinetry with hanging rods, drawers and shelves maximize every square inch and meet exact wardrobe needs.

The original bedroom had a sliding glass door that opened onto a backyard deck. The homeowners chose to remove the door to make the space private and cozy. At LJ’s Kitchens & Interiors, design is more than selecting cabinets or countertops. It’s about listening, understanding, and shaping a space that fits into your daily life seamlessly. Whether you envision something timeless and antique-inspired or sleek and modern, our designers specialize in bringing dream spaces to life.

Every space tells a story, and we design them all, including kitchens, bathrooms, living rooms, bars, mudrooms, and closets. If you can imagine it, we can design it.

As a family-owned company with more than 40 years in the Mount Pleasant community, trust and craftsmanship are at the heart of what we do. Our design team brings over 75 years of combined experience, and our work has been recognized in both regional and national publications, as well as featured in leading manufacturer catalogs. But for us, the most important recognition comes from the homeowners who trust us to transform the centerpieces of their lives.

Meet Our Team
The Experts Bringing Your Vision to Life
Scott Holmes
Scott Holmes is one of only a few Certified Kitchen Designers in the state of Michigan.

Designing spaces for his clients is truly his passion, and nothing is more satisfying than seeing a project completed and witnessing their full satisfaction. Scott’s parents, Lynn and Jerilynn, started LJ’s Kitchens & Interiors in 1976. He began working side by side with his father in 1984 and purchased the company in 1999. His dedication to guiding clients through the creation and design process is evident from the very first planning session. Scott is an active member of the National Kitchen and Bath Association and the Home Builders Association of Central Michigan.

Robert Gurski
Robert Gurski has been a designer at LJ’s Kitchen & Interiors for over 27 years.

Robert graduated from Central Michigan University 30 years ago with a bachelor degree in Interior Design and Architectural minor in Art and Art History. During his design career, he has been acknowledged in a national blog campaign; he has also won national and international awards from 20/20, the leading kitchen and bath design software, for his print of the designing process. Robert loves seeing someone’s ideas come to life in a design. He is a father of five and proud grandfather to three beautiful grandkids. When he isn’t designing kitchens and baths, he enjoys the outdoors and spending time with his wife on their small farm.

Karen Langell
Karen Langell has been a designer with LJ’s Kitchens and Interiors since graduating from Central Michigan University in 1993 with a degree in Interior Design and a minor in Art History.

She greatly enjoys working with new clients everyday on a variety of projects and being well versed in all aspects of kitchen and bathroom design. The most rewarding part of her work is taking a client’s wish list and turning a challenging room into a space they’ll love for years. It is especially rewarding to work with repeat clients who come back for more projects because they enjoyed their experience working with her. Karen is a member of the National Kitchen and Bath Association and the Home Builders Association of Central Michigan.

Megan Holmes
Megan Holmes is the third generation of the LJ’s Kitchens family.

She has worked alongside her father since 2018 to learn all aspects of the business, while also spending time learning from her paternal grandmother and mother. Family has always been at the center of her life, and she brings that same spirit to every client who walks through the doors. Her goal is to make the entire process feel easy, welcoming, and supported from start to finish. After remodeling her own home in 2019, she gained a deeper appreciation for what clients experience during design and installation. Her favorite part is bringing all the components together to make clients’ dream rooms come true. She’s an active member of the National Kitchen and Bath Association and local Home Builders Association. In her free time, she enjoys being around her family, friends and pets.

During his design career, he has been acknowledged in a national blog campaign; he has also won national and international awards from 20/20, the leading kitchen and bath design software, for his print of the designing process. Robert loves seeing someone’s ideas come to life in a design. He is a father of five and proud grandfather to three beautiful grandkids. When he isn’t designing kitchens and baths, he enjoys the outdoors and spending time with his wife on their small farm.

Karen Langell
Karen Langell has been a designer with LJ’s Kitchens and Interiors since graduating from Central Michigan University in 1993 with a degree in Interior Design and a minor in Art History.

She greatly enjoys working with new clients everyday on a variety of projects and being well versed in all aspects of kitchen and bathroom design. The most rewarding part of her work is taking a client’s wish list and turning a challenging room into a space they’ll love for years. It is especially rewarding to work with repeat clients who come back for more projects because they enjoyed their experience working with her. Karen is a member of the National Kitchen and Bath Association and the Home Builders Association of Central Michigan.

Megan Holmes
Megan Holmes is the third generation of the LJ’s Kitchens family.

She has worked alongside her father since 2018 to learn all aspects of the business, while also spending time learning from her paternal grandmother and mother. Family has always been at the center of her life, and she brings that same spirit to every client who walks through the doors. Her goal is to make the entire process feel easy, welcoming, and supported from start to finish. After remodeling her own home in 2019, she gained a deeper appreciation for what clients experience during design and installation. Her favorite part is bringing all the components together to make clients’ dream rooms come true. She’s an active member of the National Kitchen and Bath Association and local Home Builders Association. In her free time, she enjoys being around her family, friends and pets.

A Woman-Owned Hudson Valley Renovation Company Since 2008

HPM Craftsmen. A different kind of company.

HPM Craftsmen has been renovating homes in the Hudson Valley since 2008. We're based in Holmes, NY, and we work throughout Dutchess, Putnam, and Orange Counties — kitchens, bathrooms, additions, basements, and the kinds of layout changes that older homes in this region often need. Sixteen years in, we're a team of twelve people who take this work seriously.

​

We're woman-owned, which still turns heads in construction. We've never thought of it as a marketing angle — it's just who we are, and it shapes how we operate. Our clients tend to notice it in the details: the communication, the way we treat their home during a project, the fact that someone actually picks up the phone. We were featured in Hudson Valley Magazine for exactly this, and it's not something we've had to manufacture. It's how we've run jobs from the beginning.

​

The work itself matters enormously to us. We're not a company that chases volume or takes every job that comes through the door. We do renovations where craft is visible in the result — where the tile work is right, the trim is right, the addition looks like it was always there. Our clients come back to us for second and third projects, and they refer their neighbors. That's the business model we've built, and we intend to keep it.

​

What you can expect when you work with us: a clear proposal, a clean job site every day, a crew that shows up when they say they will, and honest communication if anything changes. We won't disappear after the contract is signed. The same people you meet at the consultation are the people managing your project through to the final walkthrough.

​

If you're planning a renovation in the Hudson Valley and you want to work with a team that will treat your home with the same care you do, we'd love to hear from you.
